This is not quality software, and in 2026 it is still years away from being in a state fit for consumption by paying customers. The software is riddled with bugs and performance issues that should have been caught on day one by QA.

The ATC system is unhinged. I understand that pro users address this with products like BeyondATC. I paid for the Deluxe Edition of this product, I expect a robust ATC simulation without add-ons.

The poor quality of the AI generated voices and the AI generated scripts they read (Career mode flights, for example) are immersion-breaking at best and embarrassing at worst. It is immediately obvious that zero effort was put into this aspect of the product. I should not have to acquire or purchase even more potentially paid add-ons to have realistic sounding voices with a diverse set of banter to read from.

I do not know what demographic the content in the Marketplace is intended for. At $2 - $5 each, I could see myself buying several airports that I use often. At $15 each, Microsoft is clearly telling me "we do not want your money".

Overall, this product's additions and improvements over Flight Simulator 2020 are all features that 2020 should have had on launch. What we get with 2024 is a half-baked attempt to finally 'finish' 2020, and they have still failed to hit that mark.

Perhaps Flight Simulator 2028 will present an opportunity for us to be disappointed again, but less so.

It's pretty silly to say a simulator is "like flying for real", but as someone who has spent a few dozen hours trying to get my PPL, MSFS is close enough to the real thing that I'm constantly in awe of it. The real world doesn't having melty cities that pop-in based on the limits of your video card, but it certainly models aircraft and flight dynamics pretty darn well. Want to practice stalls, touch-and-gos or autopilot and GPS systems? It's all there, and extremely faithful to what you'd get in a real plane.

As a game there's really not much to do, you have to set your own goals, but as a simulation it's fantastic. The world is there, modeled to the square foot, and just like the real thing if you don't have fun just picking a place and saying... I wanna go there... then there's not much draw.

For me, it's good enough that I really don't have much interest in flying in person anymore. I'd rather learn in a safe environment where I can check out anything from small GA planes to big airliners.

I'm giving the product a negative review for now. It is negative because I believe there significant likelihood of the average buying needing a refund after 3 hours has passed, but before they've gotten any meaningful value from the purchase. This review is meant to be a warning. Try the product on gamepass and make sure what you want to do works on your pc, in the sim, and with the peripherals you have. 

It's a pretty game and a good enough sim, but it crashes a lot. The content streaming works much better after 2 years of bake time, but it's not a perfectly functional feature yet. For example, invisible aircrafts or landmarks can occur and i believe it is due to streaming issues. 

The streaming does allow the game to occupy very little space on your PC compared to msfs 2020. Between a generous rolling cache and the 8gb install size, the harddrive footprint is 1/10 that of msfs 2020 for me. That's a decent tech accomplishment. 

Tornados only exist is only in specific missions in career mode "for now". So don't buy it for that, it's going to make you play career mode for a long time to see the tornado. You can see the tornado pretty quick on youtube. 

The career mode is welcome and fun enough. The tutorials are usefulish. Almost any youtube guide by a sim pilot do a better job getting you moving. One of the principle difficulties of starting in the sim is knowing which commands to map. The tutorials will help with that. The career tutorials really do help if you are coming in without much experience.

The mission steps in career mode are squirrelly and buggy. You are graded on mission steps and receive demerits for failure to complete them, but they aren't "smart". For instance, if you contact atc before the mission tells you too, even though it's the next step, it will not detect that you have clearance for taxi/take off. 

One frustrating scenario in career mode is that If you use the alt+n "skip to next phase of mission" feature, occasionally the scripting sets-up your plane incorrectly after the skip. For example, if you skip the taxi in the DA-40, you will not be able to achieve flight capable rpm in whatever "on" state it is in after the skip. 

These are small things, but you will frequently be searching google to find out if you are a broken pilot or if the game is broken. When the answer is both, your pain is doubled. 

It's a unique product, best on the market in many respects. A step down from msfs 2020 in some ways, but the really boring unstable tech stuff they implemented is actually cool and has the potential to be truly amazing in some future patch or edition of the game. 

If you're a sim head, you probably own it. If you're just dipping your toes, try a month of xbox game pass. It is unlikely that you will be able to troubleshoot and setup this product enough to know whether it's going to work well for you and your available peripherals within the 3 hour steam refund window. Mapping and remapping controls to preference can take an afternoon. Knowing whether simulated flight is still interesting for you after the initial fun of canyon cruising in newyork and trick flying underneath the bridges of your home city will take more than 3 hours. 

Expect greatness and frustration in equal parts at every turn. Steam should include "mixed" rating for complicated purchases like this. The refund window should be 30 days for a complex beast of software like this. Can't recommend trying on xbox gamepass emphatically enough.

One team is a team of highly professional fans who implemented stunning flight physics and incredible visual generation based on satellite imagery. This team's work can be experienced in free-flying mode and with third-party aircraft models. I utterly DO NOT RECOMEND the game for anyone wanting to try out the career mode. Because the other team is a hastily assembled crew of part-timers who, after firing all the testers, wrote the part responsible for the career mode in a terrible rush. Horrible scripts that simply ruin flights, controllers who assign flight levels 350 when the aircraft is already on a glide path intercept course, waypoints of the route in FMC from other semi-sphere the world, new career innovations like penalties for "skip" of nothing when a small mid-flight correction or ignoring a taxi route laid out across the entire airport twice  cut off around 80 percent of revenue after real-time 3 hours flight with no acceleration of time or no deliberately skipping. The economic model, where passive income only covers low-cost aircraft, which makes efforts to replenish the fleet with expensive aircraft downright unprofitable. "Special mission" assignments, given to newcomers, force virtual pilot into situations where a heavy aircraft must land in a short RWY into clearing among jungles, the final approach point being located inside a cliff.

Ich hab den Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 jetzt erst im September 2026 gekauft – und ich kann ihn wirklich nur empfehlen.
Mittlerweile hab ich über 20 Stunden gespielt und noch keinen einzigen Absturz gehabt. Das allein hat mich ehrlich gesagt schon positiv überrascht. Natürlich fehlt hier und da noch das eine oder andere Feature bzw. funktioniert noch nicht alles ganz so, wie es sollte. Aber man hat schon den Eindruck, dass Microsoft laufend daran arbeitet und der Simulator ständig weiterentwickelt wird.
Ein Beispiel sind die Helikopter: Die Rücksetzung der Trimmung funktioniert derzeit nicht wirklich fehlerfrei bzw. teilweise gar nicht. Außerdem fehlt eine Auto-Hover-Funktion, was manche Missionen mit dem Helikopter doch ziemlich schwierig machen kann. Das sind Dinge, die meiner Meinung nach noch verbessert bzw. ergänzt gehören.
Ich selbst nutze den Flight Simulator hauptsächlich für freies Fliegen, die wirklich coolen geführten Touren und fürs Sightseeing. Und genau dafür ist das Ding einfach der Hammer. Die Grafik ist genial und es macht richtig Spaß, mit dem Flugzeug quer durch die Welt zu fliegen und dabei neue Orte zu entdecken.
Über andere Features, wie zum Beispiel den Karrieremodus, kann ich allerdings nichts sagen, weil ich den bisher kaum bzw. gar nicht genutzt habe. Meine Bewertung bezieht sich daher hauptsächlich auf das freie Fliegen, die Touren und das Erkunden der Welt.
Unterm Strich bin ich rundum glücklich mit dem Kauf und hoffe, dass Microsoft den Simulator weiterhin konsequent weiterentwickelt.
Das Ding ist einfach mega, genial und riesig. 
Wer bisher überlegt hat, einzusteigen: Meiner Meinung nach zahlt es sich jetzt absolut aus.

My first flight sim ever (the closest I got was War Thunder in Realistic), and I do not regret buying it.

 The game can be gorgeous, especially while in flight - while walking it really depends on the area, obviously, there will be a lot of details missed when you try to simulate the entire Earth. I mostly fly in Free Flight, since I'm not a hardcore simulator nut, and I find the sim very relaxing to play in this way.
 I don't think there's another sim with this much variety that also looks this good and has such a large "map", the alternatives did not look so convincing for my goals.

 That being said, there is a LOT to improve in MSFS2024, so please make sure to look at other reviews before you buy. This will probably be the most demanding "game" on your system. You will also experience some bugs, and from up close you will realize that some things, like water are mostly just an illusion.
 There is also the fact that a lot of large buildings will look like melted cheeze from up close, which may be corrected by purchasing one of the thousands of mods from the marketplace. While I understand that you can't handcraft every large building that can be found on the entirety of this planet, it is still somewhat frustrating, when the perfect update for a city, sight or airport will cost you an additional few bucks. At least items often go on a discount, but I still find locking things such as powerlines or most birds you could see behind a paywall somewhat greedy.

 If that still does not discourage you, and if you are like me and you love (the idea of) exploring our planet, the different weather on it, flying in real time with real (current) weather conditions, visiting places where you would not fly IRL for one reason or another, and of course, taking screenshots of the genuinely beautiful scenery, then MSFS2024 might be for you.

There are a few good flight sims out there, but I bought this one with the career as a primary motivating factor. That said, I will base my review on the career for those others like me who are considering this game solely for that reason. If you want to buy this game to enjoy a fun and engaging career flying planes, look elsewhere. The career in this game is a massive and incredibly disappointing bust, and I will explain exactly why that is. 

For starters, and for what it's worth, it has good bones. That almost makes it worse. I have over 200 hours in the game and that is spent almost exclusively in the career so far. Initially you start out flying 'employee' contracts doing various things from sightseeing flights to skydiving contracts, and these are pretty cool, but you are barely making any money, and you need money to be able to do the missions you want to do all the time by purchasing your own planes. The game has a wide variety of planes available in free fly, but only a fraction of those are available in the career, which is itself quite frustrating, but it's not the worst part. Once you eventually save up about 20-30k doing missions that pay, at most, 4-8k and take 20 minutes to an hour to complete, you can finally purchase a Cessna Skyhawk 172. This opens up flightseeing 'freelance' missions or cargo missions if you hold out just a little longer for the higher payouts. I did cargo. This allows you to make 50k per flight instead of 4k for the same flight. You do a lot of these to save up a few hundred thousand for a vision jet to start getting passenger transport missions, netting a comfortable 250k per flight. So far so good, it takes a while but you feel like you're progressing. Then you finally do tons of those missions to save up about 4 million to buy a Cessna Grand Cherokee to do medium cargo, netting 500k per mission, but this plane is a glitchy mess. and the missions it's supposed to do are even worse. Almost every single mission has had a glitched out runway which causes a 'crash' on landing, and when flying your own planes you pay for your own repairs. This means I do a mission that takes about an hour to complete only to get a glitched runway, which I can't identify before the mission starts, and 'crash' the plane despite a perfectly smooth landing due to water or glitched holes on the runway. This costs me 100k or more to fix, so instead of making 500k for my hour long mission, I lose 100k plus fuel. The next plane that I could reasonably buy will cost 7 million or more, effectively screaching my career to a frustrating halt in which I have to decide to grind away the remaining credits, or quit the career. I chose to quit and use a 3rd party software (neofly) for a more satisfying career, but this can be used in microsoft flight simulator 2020 as well. The fact that I paid for this glitched out mess of a game because I wanted the career only to end up using an outdated 3rd party program for a much better career mode is beyond insulting. Microsoft needs to quit making 'content packs' and get their stuff together and fix this mess of a career before I will ever recommend this game to anyone interested in anything other than the free fly game mode. I may not even recommend it for that as many of the other planes in the game are glitched out messes of their own. This game feels like it was pushed out when it wasn't even halfway to completion just to score a ridiculously high price tag from poor consumers who will get hundreds of hours into the game before realizing the absolute mess that this game is, naturally far to late to demand a refund, of course.

I really wanted to love the Career Mode in this game—it was the main reason I was excited to buy MSFS—but the overall logic is fundamentally broken. The latest update just made things worse, crashing on me 3 times today alone. Do not buy this if you expect a working aviation business simulator.

Here are the MAIN points I have experienced so far during my 300+hours gameplay. There is more to it, however..

Weird Aircraft Progression & Missing Planes: The fleet choices in Career Mode make absolutely no sense. There are no "in-between" modern regional jets. Where are the promised Embraer jets, the A220, or the Dash-8 for airline service? Instead, they focus on injecting obsolete, 60-year-old planes like the Boeing 707 that nobody uses for modern career transport. Even the ATR is notoriously buggy, and the Cessna Grand Caravan—a plane used daily in real life for passenger island-hopping—is locked out of standard passenger transit in the game.

Broken Dispatch & Impossible Destinations: The mission generator is completely drunk. It will ask you to fly a fully loaded airliner across the ocean with insufficient fuel, or assign you a Honda Jet and demand you land on a 600-meter unpaved dirt strip in the Swiss Alps. It even sends you to defunct military bases in Ethiopia, only to penalize you for landing in the middle of nowhere because the airport doesn't actually exist anymore.

Suicidal ATC & Weather Avoidance: ATC will clear you for take-off with planes sitting on the runway. If there is a massive hurricane, ATC won't vector you around it; they route your Cessna straight into the storm and penalize you for it. Furthermore, you cannot request an alternate airport if your destination is socked in with zero visibility fog.

The Passenger Experience is a Joke: I spent millions on a luxury Longitude, but the game only spawns one lonely passenger. On regional 30-seater flights, the AI cabin crew demands to serve hot food literally 3 minutes before landing, and if you deny it, passenger satisfaction drops. Furthermore, passengers scream and tank your rating if you bank more than 15 degrees—even when it's physically required to line up on short final.

Missing Features & Infinite Alarms: Want to know your V1 or max flap speeds? Good luck, because many cockpits are missing basic placards and manual data. If your autopilot disconnects due to a physics glitch, the master warning alarm gets permanently stuck in an infinite, unsilenceable loop. If you request IFR taxi while the useless AI dispatcher is talking, the radio soft-locks and freezes your controls. My female co-pilot literally speaks with a deep male voice.

No Geopolitical Realism: For a "simulator," it completely ignores real-world airspace closures. You can casually fly VIP charters over active warzones in Ukraine, bypass Russian sanctions, or fly direct from Busan to Pyongyang without a care in the world.

Time Compression = Death: If you try to use the 2x sim rate, the Live Weather system randomly injects freak wind shear or "moon gravity." The autopilot panics, throws the jet into a violent death roll at FL450, and ruins hours of progress for absolutely no reason.

World Generation Bugs & AI Logic: This does not reflect the real-life world. If you fly into regional airports or dirt strips in Florida, the terrain generation is so glitched out that the runways literally look like deep canyons. Meanwhile, you'll be on short final for a massive 13,000-foot runway in Munich, just 10 feet off the ground, and ATC will force you to go around because of broken AI traffic.

It can still be fun, I still like to launch it and fly my planes around, the graphics are surreal, you can see some major cities landmarks, navigate around the Mont Blanc or admire the stars when cruising high at night.

Save your money until they actually finish developing the game and you are expecting a proper simulator from two big companies like Microsoft and Asobo. A shame it takes them almost 2 years to fix things.. 2/5

I've played this game for almost a year now. Honestly for the price its well worth it (I bought the Premium Deluxe Edition). The storage is much smaller compared to its predecessor which was way more bigger in size which is amazing for modding. To be fair the game does have its bugs (AI air traffic and Air traffic control bugs, radio bugs, and weather bugs). 

When it comes to modding you can find a wide range of aircraft (DO NOT BUY FROM MSCENERY). If your into long haul aircraft I recommend the Inibuilds A350/A330, or the PMDG 777. They are a bit pricey but if you have the money you can buy it (or you already have it depending on the version you purchased). 

If your into smaller regional jets I recommend the Inibuilds A320 and A220. As well as the PMDG 737. 

General aviation aircraft are already included and its fun to fly around places you know (like my school for example). This game is definitely a 10/10 when it comes to aviation realism and should be a avgeek's best game ever.
